objectives: 區分服務啟動與需求驗收。

sections.heading: M08-01｜能執行，不代表已驗證：如何證明軟體真的完成了？
paragraphs: 這一節最重要的觀念是：
「程式能跑」只代表它可以執行；「程式完成」則需要證據，證明它在指定條件下符合需求。
舉例來說，你請 AI 幫你開發一套醫院掛號系統。AI 告訴你：「已經完成，網站可以正常開啟。」
但這並不能證明病人真的能順利掛號、醫師不會重複預約、病歷不會被其他病人看到。
本節要學的，就是如何從「相信程式能用」，進步到「拿出可以核對的證據」。

sections.heading: 一、先用汽車理解：發得動，不等於安全可靠
paragraphs: 假設你買了一輛新車，業務員發動引擎，對你說：「車子完成檢查了，可以放心上路。」
你應該會有疑問：

- 引擎能啟動，但煞車有效嗎？
- 煞車正常，但下雨天會打滑嗎？
- 車輛正常行駛，但發生撞擊時能保護乘客嗎？
- 所有零件正常，駕駛是否看得懂儀表板？
這些都是不同的問題，必須用不同方式驗證。
軟體也是一樣。
AI 幫你產生一千行程式碼，沒有發生錯誤，網站也能打開，不代表程式符合你的需求。
這就帶出本節第一個核心觀念：
每一種品質主張，都要有對應的驗證證據。不能用一種測試通過，代替其他測試。

sections.heading: 二、軟體品質要從五個面向檢查
paragraphs: 這是整堂課最值得記住的架構。

blocks.caption: 圖 1｜需求規格與五個互補驗證面向
blocks.description: 箭頭表示從規格選擇對應的驗證問題；五個面向互補，不表示測試先後，也不能相互取代。

items.title: 需求規格（Specification）
items.body: 先說清楚：軟體應該做到什麼？

items.title: 01 啟動驗證
items.body: 程式能不能運行？

items.title: 02 規則驗證
items.body: 計算和判斷對不對？

items.title: 03 介面驗證
items.body: 操作、提示和輸出正確嗎？

items.title: 04 任務驗證
items.body: 真人能完成工作嗎？

items.title: 05 安全驗證
items.body: 不應該發生的事情，系統有沒有阻止？

paragraphs: 五個面向是互補關係，不代表必須照圖示順序測試，也不能相互取代。
### 第一層：啟動驗證（Smoke Test）
這是最基本的檢查。
例如，你開發了一家餐廳的線上訂位系統，測試人員打開網頁，發現：

- 網站正常顯示。
- 伺服器沒有當機。
- 可以看到日期及訂位按鈕。
可以說：「系統在這個測試環境成功啟動。」
但不能說：「訂位系統已經完成。」
因為你還不知道，兩個客人同時預訂最後一個位置時，會不會重複訂位。
### 第二層：規則驗證（Business Rule Testing）
這一層檢查的是業務邏輯。
以網路購物為例：
假設規格寫著：「訂單金額滿 1,000 元，運費免費。」
測試人員就必須驗證：
因為這是邊界值測試（Boundary Value Testing）。
錯誤經常發生在條件交界處。例如工程師把「大於或等於 1,000」寫成「大於 1,000」，剛好購買 1,000 元的客人就被收取運費。
這些規則測試可以用 `pytest` 等工具自動執行，但測試的好壞取決於案例是否真正涵蓋重要需求，而不是通過了多少題。
### 第三層：介面驗證（UI Testing）
即使後端計算正確，前端也可能出錯。
例如銀行轉帳系統：
後端正確判斷餘額不足，拒絕轉帳；但前端卻顯示「轉帳成功」。
這就是後端規則正確、介面行為錯誤的典型例子。
因此要檢查：使用者看見什麼訊息、按鈕何時可以使用、資料修改後畫面是否同步更新，以及下載檔案的內容是否正確。
教材提到的 Streamlit AppTest，可以模擬 Streamlit 應用程式的互動、檢查介面元件狀態。不過，AppTest 測到下載按鈕存在，不等於真實瀏覽器的下載流程及檔案內容已通過驗證。
### 第四層：使用者任務驗證（Task-based Usability Testing）
這層最容易被技術人員忽略。
假設你設計了一套醫院掛號系統，所有程式測試都通過。
但你請一位第一次使用系統的病人完成掛號，發現他不知道：

- 要先選科別還是醫師。
- 為什麼掛號按鈕無法點擊。
- 掛號完成後，在哪裡查詢結果。
這些問題不一定是程式 Bug，而是易用性（Usability）問題。
因此，任務測試不是問使用者「這套系統好不好看」，而是指定一個真實目標，觀察他能不能完成、在哪裡卡住、是否需要別人協助。
GOV.UK 的使用者研究指引也強調透過觀察實際任務理解使用障礙。
### 第五層：安全驗證（Security Testing）
假設你做了一套學生學習平台。
學生 A 登入後，可以看到自己的成績。這代表正常功能可能運作了。
但是，如果 A 只要修改網址中的學生編號，就能看到學生 B 的成績，代表系統存在授權控制問題。
這裡需要分清楚兩個專有名詞：

- Authentication（身分驗證）：確認你是誰，例如登入帳號。
- Authorization（授權）：確認你有沒有權限看這筆資料。
通過登入檢查，不代表有權限查看每一筆資料。OWASP 建議以最小權限、預設拒絕，以及針對每次請求檢查授權等方式建立控制。
而且，不能只是「測試沒有被攻破」就宣稱完全安全。必須說明測試過哪些情境、哪些防護已實作、哪些風險仍然待驗。

sections.heading: 三、最重要的思考方式：主張、證據、限制
paragraphs: 以「發票自動記帳系統」為例。
假設工程師報告：「發票功能已經完成。」
這句話太模糊了。
你應該拆成可以驗證的具體主張。
範例證據矩陣（以下均是假設情境，不是實際測試結果）

blocks.caption: 表 2｜假設情境的證據矩陣
rows: 對照已知答案的規則測試
缺漏資料被拒絕的測試
跨帳號存取遭拒的測試
所有安全風險均不存在

paragraphs: 這張表非常重要，因為它讓系統品質從「個人感覺」變成「可以審查的證據」。
我們可以進一步把它濃縮成一個原則：
完成主張 → 對應規格 → 驗證方法 → 實際結果 → 尚未涵蓋的範圍。

sections.heading: 四、把課程觀念轉換成實際開發流程
paragraphs: 教材使用 `spec.md`、測試結果，以及 `verification-notes.md` 來管理驗證紀錄。
假設我們正在開發一套文件上傳系統。
### 步驟一：先寫明確的驗收規格
不要只寫：
「使用者可以上傳文件。」
應該改成：
「當必要欄位缺漏時，系統必須顯示缺漏原因，不得產生完整報告。」
這樣才知道要測什麼。
### 步驟二：設計正常及異常情境
使用 Given–When–Then：

- Given：使用者上傳的文件缺少身分識別欄位。
- When：使用者按下「匯出報告」。
- Then：系統拒絕匯出，並提示缺漏欄位。
接著，再補上完整資料、空白資料、格式錯誤、過期資料等情境。
### 步驟三：執行測試並記下實際結果
不要只記「通過」。
至少記錄：

- 測試的程式版本（Commit）。
- 使用的環境。
- 輸入資料與預期結果。
- 真正觀察到的輸出。
- 測試狀態。
這樣其他人才能重新執行並核對。
### 步驟四：誠實區分三種狀態

blocks.caption: 圖 2｜通過、失敗與待驗
blocks.description: 三列是不同證據狀態，沒有先後關係。通過只支持已測版本與條件；沒有執行或證據不足均保留待驗。

items.title: ✓ 通過（Pass）
items.body: 已執行，結果符合預期，但只適用於已測試的版本及條件。

items.title: × 失敗（Fail）
items.body: 已執行，但觀察結果不符合預期，應保留失敗證據。

items.title: ○ 待驗（Not Tested）
items.body: 沒有執行，或缺少足夠證據，不能自行假設通過。

paragraphs: ### 步驟五：建立驗證紀錄
你可以在 `verification-notes.md` 中，留下這樣的紀錄：

blocks.heading: verification-notes.md
paragraphs: 示例尚未執行；實際結果與狀態必須在測試後更新。
blocks.code:
# 驗證紀錄

## 驗收項目
必要欄位缺漏時，不得匯出完整報告。

## 測試環境
版本：commit abc123（示例）
環境：本機測試環境

## 測試輸入
缺少身分識別欄位的合成文件。

## 預期結果
系統拒絕匯出，顯示缺漏原因。

## 實際結果
待執行測試後填寫。

## 狀態
待驗

## 下一步
執行規則測試、介面測試，
並以真實瀏覽器確認下載行為。

paragraphs: 這份紀錄最有價值的地方，不是文件寫得漂亮，而是不論誰接手，都能知道目前已經證明什麼、還缺少什麼證據。

sections.heading: 五、為什麼 AI Coding 特別需要這套方法？
paragraphs: 傳統軟體開發中，工程師可能親自編寫每一行程式，對其邏輯有一定程度的掌握。
但使用 AI Coding Agent 時，你可能只下達一段需求：
「請幫我完成發票辨識、金額核算及資料匯出功能。」
Agent 很快就修改十幾個檔案，並回答：
> Implementation completed. All tests passed.
這不等於你的需求已經驗證完成。
至少有四種可能：

1. Agent 只測試自己新增的功能，沒有測試既有功能是否壞掉。
2. 測試案例由 Agent 自己編寫，但測試沒有涵蓋真正的業務需求。
3. 測試只使用理想資料，沒有檢查異常、邊界與惡意輸入。
4. 測試在 Agent 的開發環境通過，正式環境卻存在不同設定與權限。
所以 AI 協作開發真正值得建立的是：

blocks.caption: 圖 3｜AI 協作的驗收流程
blocks.description: 箭頭表示工作與證據的承接順序；最後仍須依實際證據決定驗收、修正或保留待驗。圖示本身不是驗收結果。

items.title: 人類定義需求與驗收標準
items.body: 把完成條件寫入規格。

items.title: AI Agent 實作程式與測試
items.body: 依規格實作，涵蓋既有功能、異常與邊界。

items.title: 工具與真人蒐集驗證證據
items.body: 保留版本、環境、輸入、預期與實際結果。

items.title: 依據證據決定是否驗收、修正或保留待驗
items.body: 僅在證據支持的範圍作完成主張。

paragraphs: 這也是 M08-01 與前面 M05（規格驅動開發）及 M07（AI Coding Agent 協作）的關鍵連結：
Spec 決定什麼叫完成；Agent 負責實作；Verification 負責提出可以檢查的完成證據。

sections.heading: 六、再補一個進階觀念：Verification 與 Validation
paragraphs: 這兩個詞容易混淆。
Verification（符合規格的驗證）：我們是否把規格要求的東西做對了？
Validation（需求適切性的確認）：我們做出來的東西，是否真的滿足使用情境與使用者需求？
例如物流公司開發路線規劃系統：
系統依照規格，找出距離最短的路線。演算法測試全部通過，這是符合規格的證據。
但實際司機發現，最短路線經常有大型貨車無法通行的巷道。
因此，即使 Verification 通過，Validation 仍然可能失敗。
這不表示前面的測試毫無價值，而是說明原始需求可能沒有涵蓋真正重要的使用條件。
這個觀念能幫助我們避免一個重大陷阱：把錯誤的規格實作得非常完美。

sections.heading: 七、理解檢核：換你判斷
paragraphs: 最後記住一句話：
測試不是為了證明自己做得很好，而是為了清楚知道哪些事情已被證明、哪些事情還不能保證。
實作上，最值得養成的習慣，就是每次 AI Agent 說「完成了」，你都要求它指出：完成了哪一條需求？用什麼方式驗證？證據在哪裡？還有哪些沒有測試？

exercise.environment: spec.md、三次切片、既有測試結果與可編輯的驗證紀錄。
steps: 挑三條完成主張，分別寫出條件與對應規格。
將啟動、規則、介面、任務及多人安全證據分欄，填入實際已有結果。
指出至少一項尚無足夠證據的主張與下一個驗證動作。
exercise.expected: verification-notes.md 能區分已證明、失敗及仍待驗的範圍。
exercise.check: 每項通過都能連到相同程式版本與相關驗證，不把未測量事項推成完成。
exercise.cleanup: 停止本次啟動的服務，保留合成作品、Diff 與實際結果；不要覆蓋其他工作或留下真實資料。

en.summary: Match startup, rule, interface, task and security evidence to specific claims, identifying what is verified and what remains untested.
objectives: Distinguish service startup from requirements acceptance.
Choose sufficient, relevant evidence for quality claims.
Record actual results and verification not yet performed.

readingGuide.goal: Distinguish service startup from requirements acceptance.
readingGuide.startingPoint: spec.md, the three slices, existing test results and an editable verification record.
readingGuide.route: Understand the situation and principles, compare the workshop files, then retain verifiable operation and review records.
readingGuide.output: verification-notes.md distinguishes demonstrated, failed and still-unverified scope.

sections.heading: M08-01 | Running is not verified: how do we prove software is complete?
paragraphs: The central idea is:
“Runs” means the program can execute. “Complete” requires evidence that it meets requirements under specified conditions.
Suppose you ask AI to develop a hospital appointment system. It reports: “Complete. The website opens normally.”
That does not establish that patients can book appointments, doctors cannot be double-booked, or other patients cannot see their records.
This lesson explains how to move from trusting that software works to providing evidence someone else can check.

sections.heading: 1. A car that starts still needs safety checks
paragraphs: Suppose a salesperson starts your new car and says: “The inspection is complete. It is safe to drive.”
You still need answers:

- The engine starts, but do the brakes work?
- The brakes work, but will the car skid in rain?
- It drives normally, but will it protect passengers in a collision?
- The parts work, but can the driver understand the dashboard?
These are different questions and require different checks.
Software needs the same distinction.
AI may generate a thousand lines of code without an error and produce a website that opens. This does not establish that the software meets your requirements.
The resulting principle is:
Each quality claim needs corresponding verification evidence. Passing one kind of test cannot substitute for another.

sections.heading: 2. Check software quality from five perspectives
paragraphs: Use the following structure to choose evidence.

blocks.caption: Figure 1 | Specification and five complementary verification perspectives
blocks.description: The arrow connects the specification to relevant verification questions. The five perspectives complement one another; they are neither a testing sequence nor substitutes.

items.title: Specification
items.body: First state what the software should do.

items.title: 01 Startup verification
items.body: Can the program run?

items.title: 02 Rule verification
items.body: Are calculations and decisions correct?

items.title: 03 Interface verification
items.body: Are operations, messages and outputs correct?

items.title: 04 Task verification
items.body: Can a person complete their work?

items.title: 05 Security verification
items.body: Does the system prevent prohibited behavior?

paragraphs: The five perspectives complement one another. Their displayed order is not a mandatory testing sequence, and none substitutes for the others.
### Perspective 1: startup verification (Smoke Test)
This checks basic startup behavior.
For example, a tester opens a restaurant reservation website and observes:

- The website displays normally.
- The server has not crashed.
- A date selector and reservation button are visible.
You can report: “The system started successfully in this test environment.”
You cannot yet report: “The reservation system is complete.”
You still do not know whether two customers simultaneously booking the last available place can create a duplicate reservation.
### Perspective 2: business rule testing
This checks business logic.
Consider online shopping.
The specification says: “Orders of at least NT$1,000 qualify for free shipping.”
The tester must check:

blocks.caption: Table 1 | Free-shipping boundary values
rows: Charge according to the shipping policy

paragraphs: Why test 999, 1,000 and 1,001 specifically?
This is boundary value testing.
Errors often occur at condition boundaries. If an engineer writes “greater than 1,000” instead of “greater than or equal to 1,000,” a customer spending exactly 1,000 is incorrectly charged shipping.
Tools such as `pytest` can automate these rule tests. Their value depends on whether the cases cover important requirements, rather than the number of passing cases.
### Perspective 3: interface verification (UI Testing)
The frontend can be wrong even when backend calculations are correct.
Consider a bank transfer system.
The backend correctly detects insufficient funds and rejects a transfer, while the frontend displays “Transfer successful.”
Here, the backend rule is correct and the interface behavior is wrong.
Check what messages users see, when buttons are enabled, whether the display updates after data changes, and whether downloaded files contain the right data.

Streamlit AppTest can simulate app interactions and inspect interface element states. Finding a download button with AppTest does not establish that a real browser download and its file contents have been verified.
### Perspective 4: task-based usability testing
Technical testing can leave this perspective unexamined.
Suppose every program test for a hospital appointment system passes.
A first-time patient tries to book an appointment but does not know:

- Whether to select the department or doctor first.
- Why the booking button is disabled.
- Where to find the result after booking.
These may be usability problems rather than program bugs.
Assign a real goal and observe whether the user completes it, where they become stuck, and whether they need help. Asking whether the system looks attractive does not provide this evidence.
GOV.UK user research guidance likewise uses observation of actual tasks to identify usability barriers.
### Perspective 5: security testing
Suppose you build a student learning platform.
Student A signs in and sees their own grades. Normal functionality may be working.
If changing the student identifier in the URL lets A read student B’s grades, the system has an authorization control problem.
Distinguish these two terms:

- Authentication establishes who you are, for example through account sign-in.
- Authorization establishes whether you may access a particular record.
Passing a sign-in check does not grant access to every record. OWASP recommends least privilege, denial by default, and permission checks on every request.
A test that did not break a system does not prove complete security. State the scenarios tested, protections implemented, and risks still awaiting verification.

sections.heading: 3. Claims, evidence and limits
paragraphs: Consider an automated invoice bookkeeping system.
An engineer reports: “The invoice feature is complete.”
That statement is too vague to verify.
Break it into concrete, testable claims.
Example evidence matrix: every entry below is hypothetical, not an actual test result.
This matrix makes quality claims reviewable through evidence rather than personal impressions.
Apply this chain to each claim:
Completion claim → corresponding specification → verification method → actual result → scope not yet covered.

sections.heading: 4. Turn the concepts into a development workflow
paragraphs: Use `spec.md`, test results and `verification-notes.md` to manage verification records.
Suppose you are developing a document upload system.
### Step 1: write explicit acceptance criteria
A broad statement is:
“Users can upload documents.”
Make the acceptance behavior explicit:
“When required fields are missing, the system must explain what is missing and must not generate a complete report.”
This tells you what to test.
### Step 2: design normal and abnormal scenarios
Use Given–When–Then:

- Given: an uploaded document lacks an identity field.
- When: the user selects “Export report.”
- Then: the system rejects the export and identifies the missing field.
Add cases for complete data, blank data, malformed data and expired data.
### Step 3: run tests and record actual results
A “Pass” label alone is insufficient.
Record at least:

- The program version (commit).
- The environment used.
- Input data and expected results.
- The output actually observed.
- Test status.
These details let someone else rerun the test and check the result.
### Step 4: distinguish three evidence states

blocks.caption: Figure 2 | Pass, Fail and Not Tested
blocks.description: These rows are evidence states, not a sequence. A pass applies only to the tested version and conditions; absent execution or insufficient evidence remains Not Tested.

items.title: ✓ Pass
items.body: Executed and matched expectations, only for the tested version and conditions.

items.title: × Fail
items.body: Executed but observed results did not match expectations. Preserve failure evidence.

items.title: ○ Not Tested
items.body: Not executed, or evidence is insufficient. Do not assume a pass.

paragraphs: ### Step 5: create the verification record
You can use this example in `verification-notes.md`:

sections.heading: 5. Why AI Coding needs this discipline
paragraphs: In traditional software development, an engineer may write every line and have some direct understanding of its logic.
With an AI Coding Agent, you might provide only this request:
“Implement invoice recognition, amount calculations and data export.”
The Agent quickly changes a dozen files and replies:
> Implementation completed. All tests passed.
This does not establish that your requirements have been verified.
At least four gaps are possible:

1. The Agent tested new functionality without checking whether existing features broke.
2. The Agent wrote tests that do not cover the actual business requirements.
3. Tests use ideal data and omit abnormal, boundary and malicious inputs.
4. Tests pass in the Agent’s development environment, while production has different settings or permissions.
Establish the following collaboration workflow:

blocks.caption: Figure 3 | Acceptance in AI collaboration
blocks.description: Arrows show how work and evidence pass between responsibilities. Actual evidence determines acceptance, correction or pending verification; the diagram is not an acceptance result.

items.title: Humans define requirements and acceptance criteria
items.body: Write completion conditions into the specification.

items.title: AI Agent implements code and tests
items.body: Follow the specification and cover existing behavior, abnormal inputs and boundaries.

items.title: Tools and people collect verification evidence
items.body: Retain version, environment, inputs, expected results and actual results.

items.title: Use evidence to accept, correct or retain Not Tested
items.body: Limit completion claims to what the evidence supports.

paragraphs: This links M08-01 to M05 (specification-driven development) and M07 (AI Coding Agent collaboration):
The Spec defines completion; the Agent implements; Verification provides inspectable evidence for the completion claim.

sections.heading: 6. Verification and Validation
paragraphs: These terms address different questions.
Verification asks: have we implemented the specified requirements correctly?
Validation asks: does what we built meet the needs of users in their actual context?
Consider a logistics route planning system.
It finds the shortest route exactly as specified, and every algorithm test passes. This provides evidence of conformance to the specification.
Drivers then discover that the shortest routes often include alleys too narrow for large trucks.
Verification can therefore pass while Validation fails.
The earlier tests still have value. The original requirements may have omitted important conditions of use.
Check actual needs to avoid implementing an unsuitable specification perfectly.

sections.heading: 7. Check your understanding
paragraphs: Keep this purpose in mind:
Testing establishes what evidence supports and what remains uncertain.
Whenever an AI Agent reports “complete,” ask: which requirement is complete, how was it verified, where is the evidence, and what has not been tested?

exercise.environment: spec.md, the three slices, existing test results and an editable verification record.
steps: Choose three completion claims and specify their conditions and corresponding requirements.
Separate startup, rule, interface, task and multiuser-security evidence; enter actual existing results.
Identify at least one insufficiently supported claim and the next verification action.
exercise.expected: verification-notes.md distinguishes demonstrated, failed and still-unverified scope.

zh.prompt: 某 AI Agent 宣稱：「pytest 共有 120 個測試，全部通過。」目前最合理的結論是什麼？
options: 系統已經符合所有需求
已執行的 120 項測試符合各自預期，其他需求仍須確認
系統已經沒有安全漏洞
rationales: 測試數量沒有證明所有需求均有對應案例。
通過支持已執行的案例；需求涵蓋與其他品質面向仍須核對。
測試通過不能證明所有安全風險不存在。

en.prompt: An AI Agent reports: “All 120 pytest tests passed.” What is the most reasonable conclusion?
options: The 120 executed tests matched their expectations; other requirements still need checking
The system has no security vulnerabilities
rationales: The number of tests does not establish coverage of every requirement.
Passing supports the executed cases; requirement coverage and other quality perspectives still need checking.
Passing tests does not establish the absence of every security risk.

zh.prompt: 某學校網站能正確計算學生成績，但學生修改網址後能讀取別人的成績。這最直接屬於哪一類問題？
rationales: 問題在於取得無權讀取的資料，與美觀無關。
系統已啟動；啟動證據無法建立資料隔離。
每次資料請求仍須檢查使用者是否有權讀取該筆成績。

en.prompt: A school website calculates grades correctly, but a student changes the URL and reads someone else’s grades. What kind of problem is this most directly?
rationales: The problem is access to unauthorized data, not appearance.
The system has started; startup evidence cannot establish data isolation.
Each request must still check permission to read that grade record.

zh.prompt: 同事尚未試用新系統，但開發者認為操作流程應該很直覺。驗證紀錄該如何標示？
options: 通過，因為設計看起來合理
待驗，並安排真人任務測試
rationales: 設計推測不能代替真人任務證據。
尚未執行，保留待驗並安排具體任務觀察。
失敗需要已執行且結果不符預期的證據。

en.prompt: A colleague has not tried a new system, but its developer believes the workflow is intuitive. How should the verification record label it?
options: Pass, because the design looks reasonable
Not Tested, and arrange a real user task test
Fail, because no test was run
rationales: A design assumption cannot replace evidence from a real user task.
Execution is pending; retain Not Tested and arrange observation of a specific task.
Fail requires an executed test whose result did not match expectations.
